name: Topical clindamycin
lead: Topical clindamycin is a prescription antibiotic lotion, gel or foam used for mild to moderate acne, often combined with benzoyl peroxide or a retinoid. It is a semisynthetic derivative of lincomycin, announced in 1966 and marketed since 1968 [1].

Wikipedia reports that adding benzoyl peroxide to clindamycin works better than clindamycin alone [1]. Randomised trials from the 1990s and 2000s compared clindamycin/benzoyl peroxide gels with each component and vehicle [2][3]. Topical use commonly causes dryness, burning or peeling in over 10% of users [1].
infobox: Cleocin, Dalacin; combinations BenzaClin, Duac, Acanya, Ziana

paras: Topical clindamycin phosphate treats mild to moderate acne. Combination products include clindamycin with benzoyl peroxide (BenzaClin, Duac, Acanya) and, in the US, clindamycin with tretinoin (Ziana) [1].

Topical effects include dryness, burning, itching, scaling and contact dermatitis [1]. Systemic clindamycin raises the risk of Clostridioides difficile colitis roughly fourfold in hospital settings [1]; that figure concerns systemic use.

Clindamycin binds the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits protein synthesis [1]. Resistance is a recognised concern, and one trial rationale for combination products is suppressing resistant bacteria [4].

A pooled analysis of two double-blind trials compared clindamycin/benzoyl peroxide gel with each component and vehicle [2]. A 16-week randomised trial compared the combination with clindamycin alone for microbiologic activity and clinical efficacy [4][3]. A comparison of a foam and a gel formulation has been published [5], as have trials against nicotinamide gel [6][7] and a study of combination with adapalene [8]. Registered phase 3 trials include an adapalene-clindamycin gel (n=1617) [9] and clindamycin/benzoyl peroxide gels (n=1315, n=708) [10][11]. Detailed results are not summarised here.

card.summary: Rx antibiotic gel or lotion for mild to moderate acne, usually paired with benzoyl peroxide; well studied, with resistance a recognised concern.
card.aka: Cleocin T, Dalacin T; combos: BenzaClin, Duac, Acanya, Ziana
card.note: Resistance concerns; usually combined with benzoyl peroxide.

quick.overview:
Topical clindamycin is a prescription antibiotic for mild to moderate acne. It is usually combined with benzoyl peroxide or a retinoid.

Wikipedia reports the combination works better than clindamycin alone.
quick.mechanism: It blocks bacterial protein synthesis; combinations aim to counter resistant bacteria.
quick.risks: Dryness, burning, itching, peeling and contact dermatitis are reported in over 10% of users. Prescription-only.
